newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 18.16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 18.16 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 77 basis points to 18.16 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses a central bank formula.

The central bank said it sold 60 billion bolivars of 178-day monetary stabilization, or TEM, bills with an 18.93 percent coupon for a price of 100.35 percent. At last week's auction the six-month notes yielded 18.93 percent.

The bank also sold 20 billion bolivars of 267-day notes with a 19.36 percent coupon at a price of 99.94 percent, and 20 billion bolivars of 356-day notes with a 19.81 percent coupon at an average price of 99.50 percent.
Yields for these notes also fell -- 88 basis points to 19.45 percent for the 267-day bills, and 63 basis points to 20.42 percent for the 358-day notes.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the central bank's principal tool in setting monetary policy. The bills are used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
